route: 3 (published composite totals, exact) + 6 (keying polarity) + 7 (marker item) + 1 (cross-study per-item mean profile)
evidence: Live table via irw_fetch: 17,422 rows, 562 respondents, 31 items, resp 1-4; see verify_queiros_2018_qcae.R, VERDICT: PASS. The testable claim is that column QCAE_<n> is the S1 File's numbered Portuguese item <n>, and that resp 1..4 runs Discordo Fortemente .. Concordo Fortemente. (a) ROUTE 3, published composite totals, EXACT. Tables F of the S1 File are SPSS GLM tables for seven composites, each printing an uncorrected Total SS and a Corrected Total SS. Scoring the live items under Reniers' membership (PT = 15,16,19,20,21,22,24,25,26,27; OS = 1,3,4,5,6,18,28,30,31; EC = 8,9,13,14; PrR = 7,10,12,23; PeR = 2,11,29 with item 17 dropped) and reversing {1,2,17,29} reproduces all sixteen published numbers to the printed precision: QCAE_TOTAL 4695751 / 60192.849 (obs 4695751 / 60192.849), COGNITIVE 1953397 / 32431.788, AFFECTIVE 603834 / 15474.826, PERSPECTIVE TAKING 538857 / 13613.653, ONLINE SIMULATION 446206 / 8951.594, EMOTION CONTAGION 80490 / 2934.121, PROXIMAL RESPONSIVITY 84650 / 2614.235, PERIPHERAL RESPONSIVITY 43818 / 2958.100; largest |diff| = 0 on Total SS and 0.0004 on Corrected Total. Falsification: the same arithmetic with the response direction flipped gives QCAE_TOTAL Total SS = 2,028,451 against a published 4,695,751, so the shipped 1 = Discordo Fortemente direction is the right one. The PeR figure additionally confirms the three-item Portuguese PeR: the four-item version gives 71542 / 3319.822, which does not match. (b) ROUTE 6, keying polarity on raw scores. Correlating each raw item with its reverse-corrected subscale rest gives QCAE_1 = -0.420 (only negative of nine OS items, the rest +0.313..+0.547), QCAE_2 = -0.583 and QCAE_29 = -0.609 against QCAE_11 = +0.481 inside PeR, matching the S1 File's reverse set {1,2,17,29} and the instrument's documented 'one reverse-scored OS item, three reverse-scored PeR items'. QCAE_17 is the exception at +0.033. (c) ROUTE 7, marker item. Within reverse-scored PeR the item-rest correlations are QCAE_2 +0.583, QCAE_11 +0.481, QCAE_29 +0.609, QCAE_17 -0.033 -- QCAE_17 is uniquely and by a wide margin the item unrelated to its subscale, which is exactly the item the paper excludes from every composite 'due to an extremely low loading value'. This pins item 17 individually. (d) ROUTE 1, cross-study per-item mean profile against gomez_2022_qcae, whose numbered SPSS variable labels tie number to text independently: r = 0.770 over all 31 items, max |diff| = 0.303 (e.g. QCAE_3 3.400 vs 3.236, QCAE_20 3.235 vs 3.345, QCAE_17 2.491 vs 2.739). Against 20,000 within-subscale permutations the identity assignment beats 99.9% for Perspective Taking, 99.9% for Online Simulation, 95.9% for Emotion Contagion, 83.2% for Proximal Responsivity and 71.0% for Peripheral Responsivity. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: it does not distinguish every item from every other item. Route 3 is a SUM and is permutation-invariant WITHIN a subscale; routes 6 and 7 pin a polarity class and item 17 only; route 1 is a profile of noisy cross-sample means and is weak inside the two small affective subscales (PrR 83.2%, PeR 71.0%). Within-subscale order therefore rests on the number match between the S1 File's numbered items and the QCAE_<n> column names, corroborated but not proved by the data. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. NOT TESTED, deliberately: the S1 File's Table A per-item loadings do not reproduce in these data (Spearman 0.57 against a per-subscale CFA, with PrR item 23 published at .722 but observed at .29), so that table was not used as a route.
